Maybe it wasn't the rise to No. 3 that messed up Magic. Maybe the real problem is the name change to Amway Arena: Orlando is 3-6 since that was announced.
Magic's darling status is gone, just like that, after they followed up a magical November (12-4) with a 6-10 mark in December, including five losses at home.
With four straight home wins over sub-.500 stragglers since their four-game skid, Magic are back atop their division and tied for the East lead in wins at 21.
Road losses to Lakers, Suns showed young Magic can play with top teams. The trouble is beating them: Orlando has one win over a winning team since its 13-4 start.
At 9-15 since their 13-4 start -- and with Shaq coming back soon -- it now looks as though Magic's run as Florida's top team will wind up on the shorter side.
Ariza wasn't exactly a go-to guy for young Magic, but facts is facts: Orlando's current 1-7 nosedive to No. 7 in the East started as soon as Ariza got injured.
With Grant Hill injured anew during this 3-9 skid, you wonder now if Magic -- once miles ahead of Miami in the Fla. standings -- can even hang onto their playoff spot.
Give them this much: Magic have only four W's since Jan. 10 but they've all been impressive, especially Friday's alley-oop knifing of Spurs at the buzzer.
At 14-22 since that 13-4 start, Redick sightings are a welcome boost. For a while there, Magic were looking at two straight years getting zilch out of their lottery pick.
Magic awoke Monday down to No. 9 in the East and suddenly three games under .500. Unless they can repeat last spring's big finish, Hill might be finished as coach.
Grant Hill is returning to the lineup this week. Brian Hill is still trying to work out how Magic won 13 games from Nov. 1 to Dec. 1 and only 11 in the 13 weeks since.
On the morning of Jan. 12, Magic had the East's second-best record at 22-14. On the morning of March 12, Magic would not be in the playoffs if they started today.
Explain these trends for slumping Magic: They've won four straight against their state rivals and are 3-0 this season when going O-fer as a team from 3-point range.
This'll only be the biggest week of No. 8 Magic's season so far, with games against their two closest pursuers: No. 10 Knicks (Monday in NY) and No. 9 Pacers (Friday).
Grant Hill is playing in his first April since (gulp) 2000. He'd be in the midst of a clutch five-game winning streak, too, if Magic didn't lose both OT games last week.
Magic play four of their final six games on the road, as do Pacers. Magic haven't qualified for the playoffs since 2003, Pacers haven't missed them since 1997.
So they probably won't go ''all the way,'' as Dwight Howard optimistically proclaimed in training camp. But at least Magic didn't slip all the way out of the top eight.

sac.summary: We can't help but root for Ron-Ron, but we say this for his own good: Stop shooting. Eighteen hoists a game, three more than Kev Martin, when he's at 28.3 percent?
Bibby's playing hurt, Miller's out and Muss has to coach under a microscope. But Kings are a healthy 3-0 at home amid all the questions about their future home.
I keep getting lots of We Don't Miss Bonzi e-mails. But I'll tell you who was also glad not to see him in Kings colors Sunday night … victorious San Antonio.
Injuries, nothing new for this franchise, have made it tough to fully assess Kings, but so has this: Only two of Sacto's seven W's so far are against teams at .500 or better.
Artest (uh-oh) says he wants more shots. Bibby is gamely playing hurt but shooting 35.1 percent, 26.8 on 3s. Maybe, just maybe, Kings should look for K-Mart first.
Eight wins in November, Muss said, was ''a good month for us.'' But December? Until Joe-less Hawks came to town, it was a winless month for banged-up Kings.
A 2-7 record this month isn't a shocker given their December sked so far. The surprise is that Muss and Kings seem to be dealing with so much in-house tension already.
Artest insists that all the negative whispers in Sac are ''just false reports.'' The problem? Bibby's increasing silence and ongoing struggles suggest otherwise.
Pressing questions for 2007: Will Artest and/or Bibby last the season in Sac? And whose gold jersey will turn off more viewers: Sacramento's or Washington's?
Overtime hasn't been their time, obviously. Kings are three games under .500 and 0-3 in OT games after losing their last two at home that way (Lakers and Blazers).
Yikes. Remember when Arco Arena scared people? Now it's Kings themselves who look skittish: 1-4 at home in 2007 and 10-11 overall with four straight Arco defeats.
Panic in Sacto's kingdom is rampant with good reason. Kings' only victory in their past nine games came against the easiest team to beat these days: Boston.
That recent seven-game losing streak? It was Sacramento's longest since dropping its final seven games in 1997-98, before the days of Webber, Divac and Adelman.
If Kings play well again under Scotty Brooks, as they did in beating Denver, calls for Brooks to replace Musselman will become a Sacto staple. You watch.
With another Arco setback Sunday, Kings have the worst comparison of road wins to home losses (-5) of any team realistically in the playoff hunt. In either conference.
The last time Bibby was in a contract year, Kings went all the way to Game 7 of the Western Conference finals. Just a hunch, but I wouldn't bet on a repeat.
In the unforgiving Western Conference, these are fatal trends: Kings are 0-5 in overtime games and have racked up 11 losses by five points or fewer.
More evidence to suggest that Martin should be the focal point of the offense? He's scored 30-plus points three times in the last five games, during which Kings are 4-1.
What sort of reception awaits the reinstated Artest on the road? Ready or not, after two straight home defeats, Kings will find out six times in their next seven games.
A home-and-home with Phoenix awaits after Kings finish their five-game East trip in Atlanta. Then they've still got games against Mavs, Jazz, Rockets and at Spurs.
Kudos to Kings for stunning Suns despite losing K. Martin early. But with 40 losses overall, they've already clinched the club's worst record since going 27-55 in '97-98.
Ten games left, 5½ games out of the eighth spot and three teams closer to No. 8 than they are. In other words: Kings' run of eight straight playoff trips is done, folks.
The team Kings envy most? If they had Hornets' OT record, instead of their own 0-5 mark, Kings' run of eight straight trips to the playoffs wouldn't be ending.
Doubtful that Musselman will see this as a consolation, but last-place Kings winning at Clippers on Sunday might be what puts Muss' old team (Warriors) in the playoffs.

atl.summary: The story, for once, is not that they passed up Chris Paul. The story is that Hawks, like Paul's Hornets, are a first-place team. Someone photocopy the standings.
Joe Johnson scoffed when his coach called him an MVP candidate, but it's no exaggeration to say J.J. will get some votes if Hawks win four of every six.
Sorry. As much as I hate to say it about a team I'm pulling for, three straight home L's (two in OT and the other by a deuce) look like the start of a slide back to reality.
After 4-1 start, Hawks lost four straight by five points or fewer, three of them at home. Not the best lead-in for a stretch that calls for eight of the next 11 on the road.
Woodson probably hasn't received enough credit for Hawks hovering around .500. But they'd be an even bigger story if they hadn't lost five games by five points or less.
West Coast trip ended with a thud in Sacto, but Marvin W. is back and Hawks, who didn't have four road Ws last season until Feb. 1, are there already.
A 1-3 mark minus Joe Johnson isn't bad given how much JJ does. But Hawks' OT home loss to Bulls was their sixth in eight games decided by five points or less.
Hawks, I'm quite sure, will regret their predictable reluctance to bid for Iverson. Thanks to a 1-8 skid and with injuries galore, their annual nosedive is in full flight.
Hawks' 4-1 start suddenly looks as meaningful as Philly's 3-0 launch. They've lost five in a row by double digits since blowing a 21-point lead at home to Utah on Dec. 20.
On top of Josh's absence and a 2-12 skid overall, Joe's calf and toe have to be hurting, since he's been held to 15 points or fewer in four of his last six games.
When someone reminds you that Phoenix gets Atlanta's No. 1 pick unless Hawks finish in the lottery's top three, this 3-14 slide becomes three times as troubling.
So how do Hawks build on three straight W's? By losing twice to Bobs in 48 hours by a shameful 40 points combined, lowlighted by Josh Smith's obscene gesture.
Hawks were 6-7 in November and are 6-7 in January. Just don't ask about that 3-13 December that dropped them down into their usual spot among the stragglers.
At 9-8 in 2007 and just 3½ games out of a playoff spot, Hawks are suddenly just competitive enough to be justifiably peeved by Joe Johnson's All-Star snub.
Winning in Phoenix was sweet, even with Nash out, but don't forget that Suns will have the last laugh by inheriting Hawks' pick ... unless it's No. 1, 2 or 3.
Hawks have quietly won six of their last seven road games as part of an 8-5 uptick. They also started 4-1. The problem? In between those good times, they're 9-25.
That wacky Chuckster: Barkley lives in PHX and never seems satisfied with Suns, but works in ATL and swore back in November that Hawks would make the playoffs.
At 22-33, Hawks were flirting with respectability. But there must be something about that record because Atlanta and Charlotte both went from 22-33 to 22-38 in a hurry.
We'd love to explain this three-game winning streak without our man Joe Johnson that followed a six-game losing streak with our man Joe Johnson. But we can't.
Despite going 4-2 in their first six games without J. Johnson, Chuck Barkley's Hawks -- whom he proclaimed to be playoff-bound -- need a 15-0 finish just to hit .500.
Joe Johnson believes he'll play again this season in spite of that calf injury. The committee's rooting for him, too, since we're also nursing soccer-induced calf trouble.
It's easy to let Hawks slip from one's consciousness, but I hope the league's coaches get it right and get the versatility of lefty Josh Smith on the All-Defensive Team.
Sadly for the loyal few who follow Hawks, this ain't a new ending. Sunday's L in Philly dropped Atlanta's record since the All-Star break to 19-69 over the last three seasons.
One more Bucks loss or Hawks win clinches the league's fourth-worst record for Atlanta. Hawks' draft pick, remember, goes to Phoenix unless it's in the top three.

cha.summary: Beating Cavs was a big moment, but the most encouraging development is Okafor's fine start (13.0 ppg, 8.3 rpg, 4.3 bpg) after a worrying preseason (7.6 ppg, 5.9 rpg).
We'll get into Morrison's postgame tobacco chewing later. First, we must lament Bobcats' inability to do more with resurgent Okafor's 18.2 ppg, 12.2 rpg and 3.5 bpg.
We'd love to explain how Bobs beat Cleveland and then won in San Antonio despite losing every other game they've played. But we're busy looking for Gerald Wallace.
Bobcats awoke Monday as one of only three teams with 10 losses. The problem, obviously, is that they haven't played Cavs and Spurs often enough.
Surely you expected Bobs to beat Pistons and favor them to topple Spurs again Wednesday. They're 4-1 against CLE, SA, NJ and DET, 1-11 against all others.
Tough to enjoy Sean May's resurgence during a Spurs-Rockets-Suns home stand ... and with Okafor slowing a bit ... and with Morrison mired in a 4-for-34 slump.
Of Bobcats' six wins, make that four (somehow) against division leaders: Celtics, Spurs, Pistons and now Magic. Next up: Utah on Friday. You've been warned, Jazz.
Bobs, as promised, beat Utah to claim their fifth W this season against a division leader. Too bad Tuesday's foes in Dallas are a half-game out of Southwest lead.
When Carroll scores 27, Emeka rings up 22 and 25 and Stache comes back with 30 in Indy to complete a sweep of Lakers and Pacers, you can live with Kobe's 58.
The rookie roller-coaster continues for Morrison. Stache is suddenly playing catch-up to Matt Carroll, who, without warning, has averaged 21.8 ppg in his last four.
Now that we finally know whose team this is -- Matt Carroll's, apparently -- Carroll can't miss and Bobs have won 5 of 7, beating Lakers/Pacers/Pistons along the way.
Big week for Bobcats, who have a chance Wednesday to clinch their season series with Detroit (up 2-1) and sweep Lakers (three-OT rematch is Friday in L.A.).
You laughed when we called this Matt Carroll's team, but Bobcats are 8-7 -- and 2-0 vs. Lakers -- since Carroll's first 20-point game Dec. 29 against L.A.
Maybe we did go a bit overboard on the Matt Carroll stuff. But Bobs are still rising, at 11-8 since their 7-21 start, despite Carroll scoring just 9.4 ppg in his last five.
Figures. As soon as we praise and raise Bobcats all the way into the teens, they throw in an 0-4 week to turn an 11-8 record since that 7-21 start into 11-12.
I'm guessing Bobcats fans would prefer to see MJ at a game or two, or hear he was tutoring players at the occasional practice, as opposed to getting a letter from him.
A challenge to Mr. Morrison and every other applicable Bobcat: Charlotte is the only team left in the league that has never had a player score 45 points in a game.
Bobs have lost five in a row and still face the two toughest stops on their six-game trip: Utah and Phoenix. The good news? It's their first five-game skid all season.
MJ sits down with Bobcats TV for his first extended interview all season and reveals that his team needs a go-to guy. ''That would be a beneficial acquisition,'' MJ says.
Larry Brown admits he can't say no if MJ asks him to coach Bobs. Our question: Is an expansion team that doesn't like to spend really the best fit for Larry at this point?
If (for some reason) you rank East contenders based on how they fare vs. Bobcats, Miami clearly has an edge. Bobs are 0-2 against Heat, 2-2 vs. Pistons and Cavs.
Will this be the first 30-win season in Bobcats' history? Sean May's season is over, but Okafor is back and all Bobs need for Denny McLain territory is a 2-6 finish.
Okafor's reactivation, coupled with Herrmann's elevation to key cog w/Wallace, sparks a 5-2 surge for Bobs . . . the first to score 100 vs. Miami in Heat's last 15 games.
Bobs, like Sixers, believe late-season success means more to them than worrying about draft position. Tell us, locals: How meaningful did you find this late 7-3 rush?

por.summary: A rare mistake from the committee: Roy is wowing folks already and will remain the ROY favorite in a lot of precincts even if Blazers don't win two out of every three.
Dallas brought 'em back to Earth and Roy (for ROY) got hurt in his fourth NBA game. But tip your cap to Zach's Blazers anyway, with twice as many wins as Mavs and Suns.
Seeing Roy's foot in a boot has to be disheartening, but plucky Blazers won't let you know it. They already have comeback wins from 27, 16 and 13 points down.
Nets want no part of these upstarts. Problem is, young Blazers have no games left against New Jersey and still aren't sure when Roy will resume his ROY quest.
Ouch. Sunday's loss to Hawks completed an 0-4 homestand for back-to-Earth, Roy-less Blazers, who are 2-10 since their 4-2 start and play their next six on the road.
The anti-Bucks. Blazers have won just two of nine but it seems like more, especially with Randolph up to six 30-point, 10-rebound games, after just two last season.
The most optimistic Blazermaniacs didn't predict this: Portland has already matched last season's six road Ws and (gasp) sports a higher winning pct. than Clips do.
It's a jolly Christmas, indeed, in the PDX. Blazers have quietly posted a 6-5 record this month -- including a 4-2 road trip -- and just activated Roy (for ROY).
A 1-4 finish took some shine off Portland's surprising December, but I'm guessing Roy's return for the last six games cushions the blow somewhat. Doesn't it?
Looks like we're stuck making our usual reach, measuring Blazers and Sonics against each other and pretending that their race for regional supremacy carries meaning.
Maybe Blazers illustrate Sacramento's struggles better than anyone. Portland's only two wins in 2007? Home and home against Kings. Otherwise? Blazers are 0-6.
He's missed 20 of Portland's 42 games and might not even be Blazers' most popular rookie with Rodriguez around, but Roy could well still rank as the ROY favorite.
Randolph isn't surrendering his All-Star dream that easy, racking up some big numbers in a 5-3 spurt that already has Blazers just two W's shy of last season's 21.
Blazers' 14 straight months without a winning record is now the NBA's longest drought. The consolation: With two more W's, Blazers top last season's win total. Already.
Blazers have 22 wins already after a 21-61 season. Remembering what was expected of them, maybe Randolph is more of an All-Star snubee than I once thought.
Randolph's development and Roy's ROY lead are big stories, but the most important development in Portland might be owner Paul Allen's revived interest in his team.
The inability to trade Magloire is the secondary mystery in Blazerland. Mystery No. 1: How do they beat Jazz and Lakers back-to-back, then lose at home to Grizz?
Randolph calls team meeting! Club president resigns! Vandeweghe linked with a return as the new president! Pretty big March for a team 10 games under .500.
If you believe that Wolves are still in the hunt for the eighth spot in the West then you have to say Blazers are, too. Portland trails No. 12 Minnesota by a mere game.
With the playoffs out of range and after suffering another heavy loss to neighboring Seattle, Blazers' new priority is making sure Arenas doesn't score 50 on Tuesday.
Blazers will not manage the 12-0 finish they need to finish at .500. But Roy has the ROY locked up and they'll certainly finish above Sonics, if nothing else.
Writes Todd from Tucson: ''What was that noise last week about Portland finishing ahead of Seattle? Did the committee jinx Portland?'' Upon reflection, Todd, maybe so.
Blazers' lead over Sonics in the race for regional pride is down to a half-game. A 6-20 record in April games since April '05, furthermore, suggests this isn't their month.
The ROY trophy will be Roy's and this might already be his team. But Blazers still need a lot more, obviously, given Roy's health history and all the youth around him.

tor.summary: No shame in losing two out of three given Raps' schedule so far. The distressing part is hearing about Bosh and Tim Duncan trading plantar fasciitis stories.
This November is already better than last November, when Raps went 1-15, but Friday's home L to Hawks was hardly an uplifting prelude to a five-game trip out West.
Anyone have Villanueva going down before Ford? Not that you'll hear any gloating out of Canada, thanks to Raps' 0-4 start on their five-game trip out West.
So how does a front line of Bosh, Bargnani and Garbajosa sound? Just a hunch, but I'd say Mitchell is wise to keep moving in that direction if he wants to hang around.
Raps already have been West twice and play almost half their road schedule before Jan. 1. So maybe there is one Atlantic team that can live with its start.
A home win over Zach-less Blazers, tipping off at 10 a.m. Portland time, would have put Raps in first place in the Atlantic. But Bosh couldn't go and they couldn't get it.
Raps are this week's Seattle, winning three in a row after bad news on Bosh. Not only that, Raps are the only Titanic team with a winning record (7-3) at home.
With Nets in chaos, Pierce ailing in Boston and a helpful second-half sked, Raps have a real shot to stay right where they are. Especially after going 5-4 without Bosh.
Here's one Atlantic team with no need to apologize. Raps have played more road games than anyone (19) and are 6-6 w/out Bosh, compared to 1-11 last season.
Two weeks ago, we hinted at the idea that Raps are a legit contender for the division title. After seeing how Bosh looks post-injury, we are full-fledged believers.
Raps are a modest 4-3 since Bosh's return. But they've done the Atlantic proud this month -- no easy trick, remember -- with home near-misses against Suns and Mavs.
Of course Raps wanted to be the Atlantic's first team to reach the magical .500 mark. Then again, they're grateful just having a shot at a division title after starting 2-8.
The committee was treated to a heartwarming surprise, receiving numerous e-mails calling for one of our famous Pape Sow comments even with Raps in first place.
Two games over .500? Three-game division lead? The committee is getting ahead of ourselves, true, but can't help dreaming of Canada in the spring (and in the playoffs).
So they didn't win their road showdown with Detroit. So what? Raps are 14-6 in 2007 and rank as the Titanic's first team over .500 since New Jersey was 5-4.
We repeat: Raps don't hold the East's No. 4 seed just because they're leading the Titanic. They're No. 4 because they actually have the fourth-best record in the East.
You dare to dispute Raps' top-10 status? At 18-7, Toronto took the league's third-best record in 2007 into this week, behind only Mavs (22-2) and Suns (22-5).
February was the best month in team history: 9-3 for a .750 winning percentage. But Raps looked like they read their press clippings all weekend, starting March at 0-2.
It'll take a 14-5 finish for Raps to register the most successful season in their history. I'm guessing they'd settle for winning the Atlantic and avoiding Miami in Round 1.
Best record in franchise history update: Our Raps would need a 12-3 finish to record their first 48-win season ever. Which is asking too much, realistically.
What's the cure for Bargnani's appendectomy? An otherwise tidy 2-0 week to push Raps' division lead to 6½ games, lifting them to a season-high No. 3 in the East.
The fairy tale continues: Raps seal their first playoff spot since '02 by beating Bobs on Sunday. Their magic number to clinch the first division title in club history is three.
It just gets better and better for division-winning Raps, who even without their vital glue guy (Garbajosa) still can move up to the No. 2 seed after running over Bulls.
A mere 1-1 finish clinches the best record in franchise history. Better yet: Raps will finally get some national TV time in the playoffs so America can see how fun they are.

okc.summary: If this really is Sonics' last season in Seattle, the minimum requirement is beating out Portland in the Pacific NW standings. Yet somehow they're already playing catch-up.
Sonics had to have that one-point OT win in Atlanta. A tense locker room couldn't take another heartbreaker after losing every close game in a 1-4 start.
The momentum from Sonics' recent strong finish on an East trip didn't last, but here's something I know will get better: Ray Allen is shooting just 34.9 percent on 3s.
Sonics won more games on one East trip than they've won at home all season. Ray Allen's 3-point percentage, meanwhile, has dipped again to .322. Confused? Us, too.
Just a hunch, but I'm struggling to picture the volatile Bob Hill -- seemingly railing about something new every day -- with Sonics next season. Wherever they are.
More Ray Allen confusion. To go with that hard-to-believe percentage from 3-point range -- just .312 -- Sonics are 3-0 since Allen went down with an ankle problem.
Caution to Raps: There's a limit to winning without your star, especially with a road trip looming. After a 3-0 start sans Ray Allen, Sonics are 0-4 on a five-game excursion.
It's not so easy to celebrate Ray's return -- even though it halted a six-game losing streak -- when Rashard goes down for eight weeks just before Allen gets activated.
Rashard is out until February or March, true, but it wouldn't be all that surprising if Hill follows Fratello as the next coach to be ousted. Would it?
In November, Ray Allen shot 31.5 percent on 3-pointers. In December, 34.2 percent. First four games with the old ball? Allen is 14-for-29, good for 48.3 percent.
As if the race for All-Star spots wasn't deep enough, Ray Allen rings up 54 to A) overshadow a reborn Collison and B) put one more name in the West hopper.
It's been a streaky month -- six straight losses, followed by three straight wins -- so we can't promise that Collison will sustain his recent double-double fever.
Obviously ignoring what we think of his chances, Ray Allen is making an All-Star push, averaging 29.5 ppg in January. Trouble is, Sonics are just 4-8 this month.
Even though Ray Allen ranked as the league's top scorer in January by averaging 30.4 ppg, Hill is back on the hot seat with Sonics dropping 14 in a row on the road.
Rashard Lewis is back, Bob Hill is still feeling the heat ... and Nick Collison is overdue for a shout-out from the committee after averaging 15 and 11 in January.
Don't know how much longer we'll be able to call them Pacific Northwest rivals, but Sonics entered the break just a game behind Blazers in the regional standings.
It's official: Seattle will have at least one more season of NBA basketball. Then again, one more season like this one and last season and the locals might not miss Sonics.
Allen reveals he might need surgery, then plays on his bad ankle and scores 34 in a win over Charlotte. Guess someone had to fight back in the Year of the Injury.
Sonics quietly had assembled a look-at-us stretch -- going 8-4 -- before going East and going 0-3 with narrow losses in Philly and Toronto and a bad loss at Boston.
Satisfying as it must have been to pound Blazers for the second time in less than a month, Sonics can't easily forget that they've lost 18 games by six points or less.
Sonics' season only grows more painful: Ray Allen is done for the year and offsets his career-best scoring average (26.4 ppg) by playing a career-low 55 games.
Who knew Allen shutting it down for the season would end Minnesota's season? Ray-less Sonics soothed themselves with two comeback wins over Wolves in five days.
Didn't see this coming: Sonics are a surprising 5-6 since Allen shut it down for their season . . . with two losses by three points or less and another L in overtime.
Good thing Sonics are spending one more year in Seattle because this is no way to leave town: 50 losses is the most for this franchise since the 1985-86 season.

mem.summary: Little Kyle Lowry's 10 rebounds in his first NBA game. Rudy Gay's 21-point debut. Hakim Warrick's coming-out party. Pau-less Grizz ain't laying down, that's for sure.
The good news: Pau insists he'll be back on the busted foot before January. The reality: Whenever he returns, it'll be way too late for outmanned Grizz.
If Sunday's speculation out of Miami is true -- which tipped Fratello as the most likely Riley successor out there -- he might not mind all this ''hot seat'' talk.
You've heard lots about Pau's injury, West's and Fratello's futures and the sale of the team. The hot subject now when someone brings up Grizz? Gasol trade chatter.
Memories from any of those first-round sweeps are almost pleasant compared to looking at box scores without Pau and all the uncertainty surrounding the team's sale.
The word Jerry West likes to use is impossible. Not just to describe trying to win without Pau, but also the schedule Grizz have faced while Pau's been out injured.
Can you be happy and troubled by Pau's early return? In other words: If the June draft is as good as scouts say, would it be so bad to hold him out two more weeks?
With the sale unraveling and Grizz sliding to 2-11 this month, it was rather easy to miss Pau's 28 points, nine boards and three blocks in an OT loss to Hornets.
What a difference a year (and a healthy Pau) makes. Fratello had the NBA's fourth-best record on Dec. 26, 2005, at 16-9. Just 367 days later, Grizz had a new coach.
Grizz are certainly more offensive under Barone -- Mike Miller especially -- but didn't suffer their 27th loss last season until March 6. It's only Jan. 8, remember.
Life is naturally better with Gasol, but not exactly worlds better. Grizz went 5-17 without him and are just 4-12 with the Spaniard back from his foot injury.
Everyone says Grizz are really ready to entertain Gasol trade offers. That's fine, but I still say they were better off making a real play for Iverson to play alongside Pau.
West to New York Times: ''We have to find a star here who will attract people.'' So yet again we wonder: Why didn't Grizz make a harder push in the Iverson Sweepstakes?
The star is on the trading block. The owner is still trying to sell the team. The GM reportedly just put his house on the market. Must be fun working in Grizz ticket office.
Full disclosure that the following is a reach brought on by a case of Comment Block: Grizz take a lifetime mark of 4-2 on Valentine's Day into Wednesday's visit to Indy.
If we're cursed with Comment Block on Grizz before the trade deadline, imagine how much we'll be struggling if Gasol stays put between now and Thursday.
Yikes. Even with Mike Miller going for 45 points in Wednesday's OT loss at Golden State, Grizz are now a frightful 0-17 in the second game of back-to-backs.
Don't ask what Grizz plan to do with Pau if they get Oden or Durant. A better question, perhaps: How much more sale interest will the team generate with a top-two pick?
Can't make any promises about the lottery because the team with the worst record has only won it three times since 1990. But I feel safe saying Grizz will be that team.
More tanking trivia: Grizz are just the fourth team in NBA history with zero winning streaks through 65 games. No joke: Grizz have yet to win more than one in a row.
Uh-oh. Grizz have five games to go on a six-game trip and only 12 games left to avoid being the only team in the league this season that fails to win two in a row.
The previously unknown Tarence Kinsey sparked Grizz to their first back-to-back wins of the season . . . while making everyone wonder where he's been all season.
After posting 50, 45 and 49 wins, this is not the sort of retro move that makes folks nostalgic: Grizz are one L shy of their fifth 60-loss season in 12 years of existence.
In Canada, Grizz avoided 60 losses only twice . . . one was a 59-loss season and the other was the lockout season. But this was the first 60-loss season in Memphis.

nyk.summary: For a couple nights at least, Knicks were over .500 for the first time since early January 2005. Of course, Isiah easily could be 0-3 right now.
On top of every other crisis that keeps Knicks in the news, now Frye is backsliding further than the naysayers ever predicted, at 3.4 ppg on 22.2 percent shooting.
It had the makings of a rare week of Gotham bliss. But less than 15,000 filled MSG for the Washington rout and a home L to Boston ended their two-game win streak.
Dare we say whatever popularity Marbury restored with those $15 sneaks has been wiped out by the eight games he's registered already with less than 10 points.
Only in Gotham could this news be bad news, but Knicks -- who even Isiah admits play with 'fear' at MSG -- have only one roadie in the next 10 games.
A 2-2 start to a six-game home stand, all against sub-.500 teams, doesn't sound like much ... until you remember that Eddy Curry's Knicks were 1-6 at MSG before that.
Is this typical Knicks or what? Marbury finally goes for 31 points and eight dimes -- at MSG, no less -- but it happens at the most meaningless time: In the brawl game.
Can't promise they'll win 30 games -- even if D. Lee continues to be a rebound machine -- but we do know this: Knicks are the first team this season to play 30.
If they remember anything fondly about a calendar year marked by two brawls -- Larry vs. Isiah and Knicks vs. Nuggets -- it'll be their 3-0 record in triple-OT games in 2006.
Give it up to Isiah's Knicks . . . for once. They're 10-10 since a 5-11 start and just posted wins at Portland and Seattle after five straight double-digit road losses.
It was a short stay in the teens, true, but Knicks left us no choice by responding to our praise by giving up 126 at home in a heavy loss to banged-up Bobcats.
Right after the brawl, Knicks won two in a row (Jazz and Bobcats) at the buzzer. Last week might have been their karma payback: Back-to-back buzzer L's to Wiz, Nets.
Crawford was otherworldly with those 52 points to scorch Heat, but the league's most valuable team (according to Forbes Magazine) has dropped five of seven.
Sorry, Gotham. There were no conspiracies to keep Eddy Curry off the East All-Star team. He simply needed to rebound more and Knicks needed to win more.
You tell us, America. Knicks are five games out of the division lead and three games out of the No. 8 spot. Does that mean Isiah's playoff dream is still alive?
Still can't see Knicks cracking the top eight, but they have matched last season's win total and sit just 1½ games behind Nets in the race for local bragging rights.
I'm guessing Knicks were rooting for Nets to go ahead and trade Kidd and Carter. After Sunday's triumph, New Jersey has won 20 of the teams' last 24 encounters.
Marbury is heating up, Francis has returned from oblivion and Isiah might even be back next season. So for one week, at least, Knicks have survived the Crawford injury.
A 6-4 mark since the break doesn't exactly qualify as a ''surge.'' But you have to like Knicks' chances to make the playoffs if they stay over .500 for the final 19 games.
Evident progress? You tell me if Isiah has achieved it with losing records in November-December-January and records of 6-5 and 4-3 in February and March, respectively.
Who needs Crawford? Who needs D. Lee? Actually . . . Isiah misses both of them badly judging by Knicks' 1-5 record since he got that contract extension.
Isiah Contract Extension Update: Knicks lost four home games in March to sub-.500 teams (Sonics, Hornets, Blazers and Magic) to all but kill their playoff fantasies.
Injuries are an undeniable factor in Knicks' 3-10 slide since Isiah got his extension. But their 3-10 record against fellow Atlantic Division residents? Unpardonable.
Can't ignore all the injuries, true, but the numbers don't make for pleasant reading: Knicks are just 3-14 since Isiah's extension and only nine W's better than last season.

bos.summary: If you're tempted to say Celts never would have started 0-3 under Red, be advised that it did happen . . . once. In '50-51, Red's first season in Boston.
It hasn't lessened the serious heat Doc's facing, but Pierce wasn't kidding on that NBA TV fantasy commercial when he promised 10 boards a night. He's at 11.7 rpg.
We praise Pierce for his board work, then he stops rebounding in double digits, then Celts start winning. We'd have said something sooner if we knew the result.
Anyone else get the feeling young Celts lost focus after that three-game win streak? That's probably because last season, Boston never won more than two in a row.
On Wednesday AM, Celts led the Atlantic. By Friday PM, they had lost to Nets and Raps by a combined seven points. Now they have nine more road games this month.
Here's a question you probably wouldn't have heard a week ago: Does Doc, with Ainge's vote of confidence, now have more security than any coach in the Atlantic?
AI trade rumors might be messing with some teams, but they've reincarnated Jefferson and a Celts team that isn't exactly used to winning streaks.
Look at it this way: At least Pierce is missing a stretch that probably wasn't filled with wins anyway, with Celts going West for the first five games after Christmas.
No wins in five games since losing Pierce. No time to adjust to the old leather ball before Monday night's game in Portland. Not a very happy New Year, in other words.
Pierce returning later rather than sooner sounds like Celts' best option. Why not let Raps, Nets and Knicks ''fight'' for the Atlantic crown and play for a top-three pick?
We're running out of things to say about woebegone Celts, probably because they're running out of players and starting four guys who didn't play college ball.
Just a hunch here, but I'd say the ''confusion'' and ''mystery'' about when Pierce will return from injury just might have something to do with Celts' lottery odds.
The latest sign that winning isn't everything in Boston these days: Celts roll up a 28-10 lead on struggling Hawks at home but still fall short of 80 points and lose.
You have to go back a month for their last W: Jan. 5. My theory: Celts are convinced Red Auerbach will make sure -- from above -- that they score in the lottery this time.
Uh-oh: 23 straight L's is the single-season record. If Celts don't beat Bucks on Wed., they'll take a 19-game skid into a five-game trip out West after the break.
Celts have now won one game in the past 45 days. With 58 days to go in the regular season, what should we go with for an over/under now that Pierce is back?
We keep getting e-mails asking why Celts are lower than Grizz. Huh? Pierce might be back, but Celts arrived in Texas at 3-23 in 2007 ... and thus right where they belong.
Tied with Philly for the longest active winning streak in the East, at four in a row, is ... Boston? Next thing you'll tell me is that Al Jefferson just went for 32 and 18.
Doc Rivers recently told his team: ''[Expletive] the draft pick.'' But I'm curious to hear how Celtics fans feel right now. Happy to see this little 5-2 run? Or a bit freaked?
The law of averages says Celts were L-O-N-G overdue to beat Spurs. But don't forget, one night earlier, they almost beat Mavs in Texas, too. Team of the Week, for sure.
By following up their San Antonio breakthrough with three straight Ls, Celts have a sub-.300 winning percentage this late in the season for just the second time ever.
With Pierce, Celts are a (virtually) respectable 20-27, on pace to go 35-47 over a full season. Without Pierce, Celts are 3-23, on pace to match the mythical 9-73 mark.
Why so hard on NY for its 3-10 divisional record? Look at tanking Celts. Even in the midst of just the fifth 50-loss season in franchise history, they're 7-8 vs. Atlantic foes.
As a certain Sports Guy reminds, Sam Mitchell is winning in Toronto as a lame duck. Doc and his C's need that top-two pick way more than he needs an extension, frankly.
